newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 3 to 819 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 3 to 819 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 819 as of Oct. 4, down three from the prior week and 65 above the year-ago total of 754, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by one to 690, while rigs working offshore rose by one to 114. The number of rigs active in inland waters fell by five to 15.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed a decrease of four and Wyoming, which fell by three. New Mexico rose by two, and Kansas dipped by two.

A total of 311 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up nine from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by 12 to 503, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained unchanged at five.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 16 to 255 versus 230 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.

Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 166 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Oct. 4, up two from the prior week. The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 180, was 92.2 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean rose by one this week to 104 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 104, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count rose by two to 562 out of a total fleet of 605, making the utilization rate 92.9 percent.
